findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Split AC 17 into two: (a) the verifiable structural constraint ('no source-grep or change-detector assertions are added — verified by reviewing new test files') and (b) optionally demote the forward-looking design principle to a non-AC note or implementation guideline, since it cannot be confirmed in-session.
evidence: 'remain green under behavior-preserving refactors' is a property that can only be falsified by a future refactor, not confirmed by any command available at completion time.
The paired constraint 'no source-grep/change-detector tests are added' IS in-session verifiable by code review of the new test files.
findings.finding: AC 17 mixes an in-session-verifiable constraint ('no source-grep/change-detector tests are added') with a forward-looking design principle ('remain green under behavior-preserving refactors') that cannot be verified within the session. An agent completing this work has no deterministic in-session command that proves the forward-looking part; it is guidance, not a measurable criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'New tests are behavior/contract-focused and remain green under behavior-preserving refactors; no source-grep/change-detector tests are added.'
scenarios: An agent marks this AC green after adding well-written tests, but the 'remain green under refactors' clause is neither provable nor falsifiable during the session — making the AC's pass/fail state ambiguous.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single AC with: (a) '[ ] No new test uses source-file grep, internal symbol name matching, or change-detector assertions — confirmed by code review of added test files.' and move 'remain green under behavior-preserving refactors' to the Test Design section as an authoring guideline rather than an acceptance criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For each of `reason_grounded` and `repo_file_change_named`, either (a) add a co-located decision rule that uses the field value (e.g. `reason_grounded: no` + `assertion_plausible: insufficient` → stronger coaching; `repo_file_change_named: yes` + `assertion_plausible: insufficient` → promote to advisory contradiction), or (b) remove the field from the sub-answer schema if it carries no decision role.
evidence: Plan declares: 'assertion_plausible: yes|no|insufficient', 'reason_grounded: yes|no', 'repo_file_change_named: yes|no'
All three decision rules (yes → PASS, no → advisory contradiction, insufficient → coaching) branch on `assertion_plausible` only
`reason_grounded` and `repo_file_change_named` appear nowhere in the decision rules or output contract

Analogous prompts (plan_review_asserted_capability.md, plan_review_necessity.md, plan_review_decomp_shape.md) define only fields that each appear in a named decision rule — no orphaned schema keys exist in those files
findings.finding: `reason_grounded` and `repo_file_change_named` are declared as CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWER fields in the criterion schema but their roles in the decision protocol are never specified anywhere in the plan. The three decision rules branch exclusively on `assertion_plausible`; neither `reason_grounded` nor `repo_file_change_named` appears in any rule, coaching instruction, or output contract. An executor filling these fields has no protocol for how the values affect the criterion's output.
findings.location: Plan section 'Criterion judgment and prompt discovery' — CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS definition and decision rules
scenarios: An executor sets `reason_grounded: no` (the declared reason is ungrounded) but `assertion_plausible: yes` — the decision rules say PASS, silently ignoring the ungrounded reason signal
An executor sets `repo_file_change_named: yes` but `assertion_plausible: insufficient` — the coaching output is the same as if no file was named, wasting a strong signal
A test asserting the sub-answer contract has no protocol to validate the field values against, making it impossible to specify a meaningful oracle
findings.suggested_fix: If the intended semantics are: `repo_file_change_named: yes` overrides `insufficient` to `no` (a named file change is a plausibility signal strong enough to fire), add that rule explicitly. If `reason_grounded: no` tightens the `insufficient` coaching, state that. Otherwise remove the orphaned fields.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the premise in 'Declared-reason data flow': acknowledge that `pass1.py` currently has only a hardcoded G5 check for `extra_context`, not a generic per-criterion dispatch, and specify whether the implementation should (a) generalise the G5 check into a criterion-keyed dispatch table and then add `no-file-impact`, or (b) add a second hardcoded check analogous to the G5 one.
evidence: Plan says: 'Extend the existing per-criterion `extra_context` construction in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` so a chunk containing `no-file-impact` receives this exact Markdown section'
pass1.py:418: `extra = decomp_context if any(c.get('id') == 'G5' for c in chunk) else ''` — a single hardcoded G5 check, not a per-criterion dispatch table
No search results for 'per-criterion extra_context' in the codebase
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'Extend the existing per-criterion `extra_context` construction in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py`' as though a generic per-criterion extra_context dispatch mechanism already exists. The actual code contains only a single hardcoded G5 check (`extra = decomp_context if any(c.get('id') == 'G5' for c in chunk) else ''`) with no generalised per-criterion extra_context dispatch. The plan must instead describe creating this mechanism (not just extending it), since the `no-file-impact` criterion would be the second special case and will need its own chunk-level detection logic analogous to the G5 path.
findings.location: Approach section: 'Declared-reason data flow' / pass1.py lines 416-421
scenarios: An implementer reads 'extend the existing per-criterion construction' and looks for a dispatch table or registry to add an entry to — finds none, causing confusion about where to add the new special case.

If the implementer adds a second hardcoded check for 'no-file-impact' alongside the G5 check without generalising the pattern, the pass1.py logic becomes an unmaintainable series of `if any(c.get('id') == 'X') for c in chunk)` guards — the plan's framing implies a cleaner extension point exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'Extend the existing per-criterion `extra_context` construction' with 'Add a second per-criterion extra-context injection point alongside the existing G5 check, following the same pattern: `extra = (declared_reason_block if any(c.get("id") == "no-file-impact" for c in chunk) else "") or (decomp_context if any(c.get("id") == "G5" for c in chunk) else "")`.' Alternatively, generalise to a criterion-keyed dict.

A maintainer reviewing the routing JSON cannot validate the key against any documented schema
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Routing keys reference' section (or extend the existing one) in AGENTS.md or docs/ listing `require_file_impact_scope` alongside `require_parent_id`, with accepted type (non-empty list of strings), semantics (criterion selected only when persisted scope is a member), and the fail-closed contract for missing/None values.

findings.suggested_fix: In `pass1.py`, wrap the LLM call for each criterion so that any exception or fail-open fallback emits a structured log line at WARNING level including `criterion=no-file-impact`, `outcome=fail_open`, and the exception class. Confirm this already happens in the shared framework, or add it explicitly for this criterion. Add an AC: 'A transient LLM error for no-file-impact produces a structured WARNING log entry and does not block claim.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether `require_file_impact_scope` as a generalized routing key in `overlay.py`/`registry.applies()` is justified over a T8-style hardcode in `route_criteria` (e.g. `if cid == 'no-file-impact' and ctx.state.get('file_impact_scope') != 'none': continue`) — the T8 pattern handles a single-criterion scope gate without touching the shared overlay schema.
evidence: Plan proposes `applies_at.require_file_impact_scope: ["none"]` validated in overlay.py and evaluated in registry.applies() — a new key type with no existing consumers.

Existing T8 special-case in route_criteria (registry.py:386-387): `if cid == 'T8' and not registry.t8_llm_surface_applies(plan): continue` — a hardcoded single-criterion gate that does not touch overlay.py or applies().
`require_parent_id` has exactly one consumer (G7) and is the stated precedent, but that key already exists in production; the new key has 0 call-sites.
Rule-of-Three: 0 existing consumers of `require_file_impact_scope`; 1 planned.
findings.finding: The new `require_file_impact_scope` applies_at routing key is a premature abstraction with exactly 0 existing consumers and 1 planned consumer (`no-file-impact`), while a simpler single-criterion gate already exists in `route_criteria` (the T8 pattern: `if cid == 'T8' and not registry.t8_llm_surface_applies(plan): continue`). The plan chooses the heavier path — new key validation in `overlay.py`, new keyword argument and predicate logic in `registry.applies()` — over a two-line hardcode in `route_criteria`, contaminating the shared routing schema for a single consumer.
scenarios: A future criterion author encounters `require_file_impact_scope` in overlay.py docs and assumes it is a general-purpose ticket-state filter pattern, adding new criteria with `require_file_impact_scope: ["paths"]` etc. before there is a proven need.
The additional validation path in overlay.py must be maintained for future routing-schema changes even if no second consumer ever materializes.
findings.suggested_fix: In `route_criteria`, add a two-line hardcode analogous to the T8 gate: `if cid == 'no-file-impact' and ctx.state.get('file_impact_scope') != 'none': continue`. This avoids the new `overlay.py` validation key and the `file_impact_scope` keyword on `registry.applies()` entirely, at the cost of the criterion's applicability not being expressible declaratively in the routing entry — an acceptable trade-off given there is only one consumer.

findings.finding: The plan omits `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` from its Scope and AC list, but this file contains the static `criteria:` list that drives the `ProductionBatchRunner` batch step. Every BUILT-IN criterion that runs via the production workflow must have a `- prompt: plan-review-<id> / when: ${{ steps.assemble.outputs.include_<id> }}` entry there. The plan adds `no-file-impact` to `CANONICAL_LLM` and `criteria_routing.json`, but without a YAML entry the criterion will never be dispatched to the `ProductionBatchRunner` in the live workflow (it will only run through the bespoke orchestrator path, if that is still active).
scenarios: The no-file-impact criterion is added to CANONICAL_LLM, routing.json, registry.py, pass1.py — but the production gate YAML batch step never dispatches it, so it silently never runs on any ticket in production.

If the pre-existing pattern (removal-rationale etc. also missing from YAML) is intentional and these criteria are known to not run via the production workflow, the plan should at least acknowledge this.

There is no described test that exercises the rubric's third outcome.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC5 / Test Design — 'Offline rubric behavior'
